mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a low FEDFUNDS period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 6% signals labor market weakness, which may lead to economic downturns and negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 exhibits positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods after UNRATE exceeds 6%, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with low unemployment indicates a robust economy, which is likely to drive corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following strong GDP growth and low unemployment, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, high federal funds rates increase borrowing costs and reduce consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods during a monetary tightening cycle with high FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in retail sales indicates strong consumer demand, which is likely to boost corporate revenues and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 5-day windows following retail sales growth, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below a certain threshold signals supply-side weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as production cuts and reduced economic activity impact corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 exhibits positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day periods following an INDPRO decline below 110, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation coupled with low unemployment may lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing consumer and business spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following high inflation and low unemployment, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth in a low unemployment regime indicates a robust labor market, which is likely to drive consumer spending and business investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following strong employment growth in a low unemployment regime, the hypothesis is invalidated.
